thread:
emma: Heads up — customer using our hosted SSE stream (chat completions) reports the client gets a silent close mid-stream when the app is backgrounded and the phone switches from cellular->WiFi. No 5xx from our side in the logs. iOS 16.6, app uses our iOS SDK v1.8.2. Repro steps attached.

alex: rough repro steps? can we reproduce locally with a network switch emulator?

emma: Steps we have so far:
- Start streaming completion (long response, ~1.2k tokens) on iPhone (app in foreground)
- Put app to background via home button (so app background tasks)
- Toggle WiFi on (was on LTE) or switch to a wifi network (carrier->wifi)
- Client receives 'close' event and stream stops producing more chunks, no final done.
- No 502/503 on our edge. Connection from client disappears in proxy logs.

maria: do we have client side logs? what does the SDK report?

emma: client log snippet: 
```
SSEClient: onmessage chunk id=34
SSEClient: onmessage chunk id=35
SSEClient: connection closed (code=0)
SSEClient: onclose event (reason="" )
```
No mention of HTTP error, just close.

alex: interesting. Could be the iOS TCP stack aborting sockets when backgrounding + network change. iOS sometimes kills long-lived sockets to conserve. Did they enable background network mode?

emma: customer says they didn't request special background modes. They want the stream to resume or at least a graceful error.

sam: quick question — are we sending regular SSE comment pings? keepalive? Some mobile proxies kill idle connections if no data in X seconds.

emma: our default keepalive is a comment every 30s for streams. Logs show last keepalive at t=+90s, then it stops when the switch happens.

maria: can you paste the proxy logs around the time of disconnect?

emma: proxy tail: 
```
[2024-04-01T12:03:14Z] conn_id=abc123 client=10.3.45.67 upstream=10.8.9.2 state=streaming last_event=chunk id=35
[2024-04-01T12:03:56Z] conn_id=abc123 client=10.3.45.67 tcp_reset_from_client
[2024-04-01T12:03:56Z] conn_id=abc123 upstream=10.8.9.2 closed_by_client
```
No 5xx, just client-side reset.

alex: that fits TCP RST from the device when moving networks. On iOS background network behavior: if app isn't registered for background transfers, the OS can close sockets. Some carriers also break NAT pinholes when switching.

sam: can we detect and surface a different event to the SDK so app can attempt resume? e.g., send a brief final SSE event before we close? But we don't control client-side OS killing the socket.

emma: customer asks if we can support resumable streams (last-event-id / range resume) for long-running SSE responses.

maria: we don't currently support resume semantics for chat streams. Could consider adding a server-side resume token that increments per chunk and an endpoint to resume from token. That'd be design work.

alex: immediate workaround: SDK should detect backgrounding and either (a) cancel the stream with a clean close so app gets an error it can surface, or (b) use shorter chunked responses and request smaller completions. Also reduce reliance on very long single-stream responses.

emma: we should give the customer repro steps to confirm it's client-side. Suggest running curl from laptop and toggling network? but they reported only mobile repro. We need a way to repro deterministically.

sam: here's a quick curl-based repro that simulates a network-level close:
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=longform" \
  --no-buffer --max-time 300
# then disable the NIC to simulate abrupt client close
```
This will show that if the client resets socket, server sees a FIN/RST and can't complete.

maria: also ask them to try toggling WiFi in airplane-mode on/off to see if the same close occurs. If it's always an abrupt TCP reset from client-side, it's not a server bug.

emma: customer also pasted SDK network trace (CFNetwork): 
```
TCP FIN_WAIT_2 -> TIME_WAIT
CFURLSessionStreamTask: connection closed while backgrounding
```

alex: another datapoint — do we rotate TLS session or auth mid-stream? Token expiry could lead to mid-stream close but that'd be 401/403. You said no 4xx.

emma: right, no auth errors. Token valid for duration.

sam: propose we add to response headers a lightweight resume-id in case we later support resume, and instrument SDK to log background events and emit a more descriptive error when the socket is killed.

maria: agree. Quick action items for triage: 
1) Ask customer to reproduce with SDK debug logs and full network trace (pcap) if possible.
2) Suggest SDK change: on app background, send an explicit close event (soft close) and mark stream as resumable UI-wise.
3) Product: evaluate resumability feature (server-side token + resume endpoint).

emma: ping @sam can you draft the SDK PR text for the workaround (detect background + send client-cancel)?

sam: yeah I'll draft. Short-term we can add a note to support KB: "SSE streams may be closed by mobile OS during network transitions; best practices: implement client-side resume/cancel logic, smaller completions, and enable keepalives."

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: sdk/1.8.3 -> staged (notes: add more verbose background logs) :thumbsup:

alex: OK, final reply to customer should summarize: likely OS-level socket reset on network change, not server error; steps to workaround; offer to test with an internal build of new SDK logs; ask for pcap if they can capture.

emma: sending reply to customer with those steps now. I'll follow up if they can capture a pcap. Thanks all. :handshake:
